text:
Really fascinated by Sprout's headspace and was wondering if you had any insight to it. From my reading Sprout has some severe self esteem issues. He walks Cosmo around on a leash to impose this sense of dominance yet at the expense of being controlled for greater means. He knows he's playing a facade yet never admits it, even when confronted with it (like when Astro calls him out on his power imbalance with Cosmo. 
A part of this episode that really struck me as interesting was when sprout said he "is tired of everyone liking dandy more than him" because it's just blatently not true. We see time and time again that the residents of Gardenview detest dandy - dandy himself even refers to sprout as the "most popular toon in gardenview." Yet somehow sprout can't see that, and consistently views himself as lesser than dandy, perhaps out of admiration or a fuel for their rivalry.
Another part was Cosmo's statement about how they were made for one another, reinforcing this idea that Sprout is not capable of being his own person. He is only known around town because of his association with Cosmo, but without him he fears he would be a nobody. 

Feel totally free to correct me if I'm wrong on my analysis, but if I'm not I would LOVE to see this aspect expanded on more. Sprout has always been my favorite from this series, and I love this new angle we're seeing of him in this episode ❤❤❤ keep up the good work!

text:
Just finished my third watching of this episode- this might be your best video yet, and I've been subscribed since Sonic Underground on your first channel. Sprout's experience of working on his birthday and going to a party that he doesnt even want to go to right after is super relatable, the moment where they're putting birthday candles on his cake and giving him a little wish with each one is super cute, and the drama, the comedy, the action, the resolution, it's all so so good. Those Twisted designs look SO good in your art style. On twitter you recently said it takes too long to draw the twisted forms, and looking at a scene like 18:59 where you had to animate this quadruped walking animation I can 100% see where you're coming from, it just seems so complicated to move every limb around in a full body shot. I've noticed in most instances with Dandy's twisted form you tend to use close-up shots, perhaps to avoid having to animate his whole body, which adds this kind of mystery to his Twisted form. In the beach episode where he "extracts ichor" from Astro's eye using his Twisted Form, the lack of a full body shot makes him look gigantic, really selling how dominating his presence is in that scene. It's really cool how you use these kind of "perspective tricks" and "camera angles" to work around these constraints. Of course, since you used a full body shot for his twisted form in this episode, he looks much smaller than normal, which only compliments the fact that he lost since he's not as intimidating by comparison !

Seeing Dandy buck broken and defeated is SUCH good development. Much like the recent Halloween episode where Dyle forces a kiss on Dandy, it's these moments of weakness and vulnerability that really creates this awesome characterization for our flowery boy. I will say, as a viewer, i think the reason why Dandy lost is because Sprout and Cosmo were working as a team, since they're boyfriends (or "best friends") and all that, meanwhile Dandy and Astro weren't working together. It kind of gets at the fact that Astro and Dandy aren't really "together" like Cosmo and Sprout, but I would bet if they ever were to make their relationship official, that could act as a sort of symbolic boost to their coordination in a fight, and they could easily win a 2v2 rematch.

You also had some Soulvester and Gourdy moments which are my absolute favorites! I recently subbed on Patreon (Sneedster) and my only regret is that I didn't do it sooner!
